gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the four makers measure their fast-charge times differently. Anker's 49-minute figure for the C1000 Gen 2 is 0–100% and only works after you turn on UltraFast in the Anker app, and Anker advises using it only when necessary to prolong battery lifespan. BLUETTI's Elite 100 V2 and EcoFlow's DELTA 3 Classic quote 45 minutes to 80%, not to full. Jackery's own FAQ gives the Explorer 1000 v2 a single AC time of about 1.7 hours and lists the app's emergency charging mode as 'Not supported'.
standout_why: I compared against backup-power.org/best-1000wh-power-stations (cited in one chat) and thepowerstationguide.com/blog/best-1000wh-portable-power-stations (cited in another). Both already flag that Jackery rates cycle life to 70% while the others rate to 80%, so that footnote is not new. backup-power.org also already notes that BLUETTI's 2,700 W is Power Lifting for resistive loads, not motor-start surge. Neither page puts the charge times on the same footing: one quotes 0–80% and the others 0–100%, and neither says Anker's 49 minutes needs a setting turned on in the app or that Jackery's FAQ lists no app emergency mode. I could not open enoughwatts.com/power-stations/size/1000-wh, the most-cited rival (SSL error), so I could not check it for this.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. The Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 is still the fastest to recharge from empty to full, but only when you choose to turn on UltraFast in the app. BLUETTI and EcoFlow's '45 minutes' covers 80%, and full is longer. The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 is clearly the slowest from the wall (about 1.7 h) and also has the weakest cycle rating (4,000 cycles to 70% against the others' 80%). That makes it a carry-weight pick (23.8 lb) rather than a home-backup pick. For someone who means 1,000 W of output, BLUETTI's 2,700 W 'Lifting' figure is not surge; going by the maker pages I could open, the C1000 Gen 2's 2,000 W continuous is the highest.
